# Test plan

*Generated by `homelab testplan` from the test sources. Do not edit by hand: the next run overwrites it, and a test checks that the committed copy is current.*

**950 tests in 83 integration-test suites.**

## How this document is made

Every statement below is read out of a file, not written beside it:

- **What a suite is for** is the first paragraph of the `//!` comment at the top of its file.
- **What a test checks** is its function name, which in this codebase is written as a sentence, followed by the first sentence of its `///` comment when it has one.
- **Which finding a test pins** comes from a `/// covers: <id>` line above it. The one-line description of each id is the title of that row in `docs/deployment/REGISTER.md`.
- **Accepted limitations** are the rows of the gap table in `docs/deployment/REALIZATION_PLAN.md` whose status is *later*.

A test that is deleted or renamed disappears from this document on the next run.

## Scope

Described here: every test in the integration-test directories `core/tests` and `client/tests`.

Counted but not described: the 98 unit tests inside the workspace crates' own `src/` trees (`core/src` 10, `proto/src` 3, `host/src` 69, `client/src` 12, `admin/src` 4). They run with `cargo test --workspace` like the rest; this document does not read them.

## Running the tests

```sh
# the whole workspace, as .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it
cargo test --workspace --locked
# one crate
cargo test -p homelab-core
cargo test -p homelab-client
# one suite, named after its file
cargo test -p homelab-core --test argv_secret_tests
```

### auto_park_tests

`core/tests/auto_park_tests.rs` · 2 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test auto_park_tests`

gap-22: the automatic-park notice says what the automatic park does.

Tests:

- `gap_22_the_auto_park_notice_does_not_claim_onboot_was_cleared`
- `fix_59_a_failed_night_never_stops_the_stacks_backups`: fix-59 (failed-update-parks-backups, 2026-09-27): one bad upstream image, or one Drive 5xx at the backup hour, set `enabled = false`, and a disabled stack gets no nightly backup until somebody types `homelab enable`.

### busy_tests

`core/tests/busy_tests.rs` · 13 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test busy_tests`

O10: the check that keeps an update out of somebody's evening.

Tests:

- `o10_a_paused_film_still_counts_as_busy`: The real answer when somebody has a film open and paused.
- `o10_open_but_idle_sessions_do_not_block`: Sessions open but nothing playing: an idle browser tab is not an evening.
- `o10_nobody_connected_allows_the_update`
- `o10_every_uncertain_answer_blocks_the_update`: The heart of it.
- `o10_the_v1_field_is_not_what_decides`: A field that does not exist cannot be a test.
- `o10_an_app_that_does_not_ask_is_not_questioned`: An app that carries no label is never asked — one call, not two.
- `o10_dockers_word_for_absent_is_not_a_check_name`: `docker inspect` prints `<no value>` for a label that is not there, and a non-empty string that means "absent" is exactly the kind of value that reads as present.
- `o10_an_unknown_check_name_counts_as_in_use`: A label naming a check nobody implemented fails closed rather than silently allowing the stop.
- `o10_a_watching_session_is_seen_through_the_shared_probe`
- `a_deferred_night_neither_parks_the_stack_nor_records_a_backup`
- `a_real_failure_still_parks_and_a_good_night_still_records`
- `fix_60_no_automatic_update_without_tonights_backup`: fix-60 (updates-run-after-failed-backup, 2026-09-27): the scheduler ran every automatic update after the backup batch whatever the backup did.
- `the_worst_service_decides_the_stacks_night`: T5: services sharing one container share a fate.

### checks_tests

`core/tests/checks_tests.rs` · 12 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test checks_tests`

J1-J3: the before/after pair, and why there are no thresholds in it.

Findings these tests pin:

- **F156**: The TUI reaches nine of the twenty-five operations the host can perform.

Tests:

- `j1_a_count_may_rise_and_must_not_fall`: Kenny's objection, as a test.
- `j1_the_pair_needs_no_tolerance_because_it_is_taken_minutes_apart`: The media rebuild is the case: the downloader was importing throughout, so "equal" would have failed a healthy rebuild and "at least N" would have been a guess about a library that changes hourly.
- `must_match_catches_a_changed_setting`: Configuration is not content: a library path or a transcoding device that changed is a fault even though nothing got smaller.
- `fix_151_a_must_match_check_with_no_reading_before_takes_its_first_reading_as_the_baseline`: fix-151 (2026-09-28, the metrics deploy that moved Loki and Grafana onto CT 113): a `must_match` check whose BEFORE reading is empty — the app did not exist on this container yet — has nothing to match against.
- `an_unreadable_measurement_is_not_a_regression`: A command that will not run says nothing about the data.
- `a_first_deploy_has_nothing_to_compare_and_passes`: A fresh container has no before.
- `blind_spots_are_reported_with_a_green_result`: The blind spots come back even when everything passed, because that is exactly the moment nobody asks what was not checked.
- `a_service_whose_deepest_check_is_a_port_is_refused`: Kenny's challenge, as a rule rather than an intention.
- `a_shallow_check_must_declare_its_blind_spot`: And a shallow check must say what it does not prove, because that is exactly the one that gets mistaken for proof.
- `a_service_without_checks_is_not_nagged`: A service with no checks at all is not judged.
- `a_question_nobody_answers_never_reads_as_permission`: The answer that matters most is the one nobody gives.
- `a_deliberate_drop_can_be_allowed_but_never_by_silence`: T69, the half that matters: the mechanism is actually wired to the case Kenny named. *(pins F156)*

### compose_policy_tests

`core/tests/compose_policy_tests.rs` · 4 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test compose_policy_tests`

fix-117 (compose-policy-first-container, 2026-09-27): the automatic update read `com.homelab.update.policy` from the app's FIRST container and applied it to the whole app. `stacks/paperwork/paperless-db` labels postgres `manual` and redis `auto`: depending on container order, Postgres got the nightly recreate its label forbids, or redis never updated.

Tests:

- `the_scope_is_read_per_service`
- `a_mixed_app_updates_only_its_auto_services`
- `the_order_of_the_containers_decides_nothing`

### compose_verify_tests

`core/tests/compose_verify_tests.rs` · 4 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test compose_verify_tests`

fix-118 (compose-update-verify-weak, 2026-09-27): the compose update's verify asked "did one service start", read once right after `up -d`. A two-service app with a crashed Postgres, or a container in a restart loop that is `running` part of each cycle, passed as a good update. F300 fixed exactly this for native units; this ports it.

Tests:

- `the_settle_check_ports_f300`
- `a_restart_loop_after_the_update_is_rolled_back`
- `a_new_image_that_settles_is_kept`
- `an_unchanged_image_does_not_wait_a_settle_window`

### declarative_cleanup_tests

`core/tests/declarative_cleanup_tests.rs` · 27 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test declarative_cleanup_tests`

step-22 / ask-8 (Kenny, 2026-09-27): everything a stack registers is declarative. What the files declare is added; what leaves them is removed.

Findings these tests pin:

- **ask-8**: Declarative cleanup where data or a container is involved.
- **ask-9**: Backups, /appdata and vault copies of a destroyed stack are kept forever; wiping them is an explicit act, never automatic, and their existence is brought to (...)
- **fix-41**: Two regressions from the same day's declarative cleanup (v3.59.0), found by the expert panel before either fired.
- **step-22**: Audit of every place a stack registers itself, against the declarative principle (2026-09-27).

Tests:

- `forget_unregisters_everything_a_destroy_unregisters`: `homelab forget` dropped the state record and nothing else, so a stack forgotten after its container was lost kept its route, its scrape target, its dashboard, its manual checks, its tile and its host monitor. *(pins step-22)*
- `forget_still_refuses_a_record_whose_container_is_live`: The one guard forget always had stays: a record whose container still answers is live, and nothing about it is unregistered. *(pins step-22)*
- `destroy_drops_the_manual_checks_and_regenerates_the_fleet_files` *(pins step-22)*
- `a_stack_that_drops_its_gateway_route_loses_the_route_file` *(pins step-22)*
- `a_stack_that_moves_to_another_vmid_loses_the_old_route_file` *(pins step-22)*
- `a_hand_written_route_file_is_never_retired`: fix-41: the route retirement removed `<vmid>-app-<stack>.yml` for any stack without a `gateway_route`, including a route written by hand on the gateway: almanac's `112-app-almanac.yml` would have gone on its next deploy, and almanac.kp-soft.dev with it (found by the network reviewer, 2026-09-27). *(pins fix-41)*
- `a_deploy_records_the_route_file_it_wrote`: fix-41: a deploy records the route file it wrote, so a later drop can retire exactly that file. *(pins fix-41)*
- `the_intent_repo_copy_loses_files_the_stack_no_longer_has` *(pins step-22)*
- `the_fleet_check_reports_a_stack_in_state_without_a_stack_file` *(pins ask-8, step-22)*
- `destroy_works_from_the_manifest_recorded_in_state`: `homelab apply` destroys a stack whose directory is gone, so destroy has to work without the directory: from `StackState.manifest`, behind the same typed name, no-touch list and hostname guard. *(pins ask-8)*
- `destroy_from_state_keeps_every_safety_gate` *(pins ask-8)*
- `the_deploy_removes_files_the_stack_no_longer_declares`: D84 reported orphans and left them for `homelab prune-orphans`; ask-8 (`Automatisch bij deploy`) has the deploy remove them, one line each. *(pins ask-8)*
- `generated_dashboards_on_the_gateway_are_never_orphans`: Files the orchestrator writes into a container on behalf of OTHER stacks (generated dashboards on the gateway) are not the gateway's orphans. *(pins ask-8)*
- `a_dropped_rootfs_unit_is_disabled_then_removed_then_reloaded`: A `rootfs/` file the stack used to place (known from the intent repo's previous copy) is removed from the container; a unit or timer is disabled and stopped first, and systemd is reloaded afterwards. *(pins ask-8)*
- `a_native_unit_dropped_from_the_stack_is_stopped_and_unregistered_with_its_data_kept`: `Stoppen, data bewaren`: stopped, disabled, unit file and program removed, out of state; data dirs and the restic repository stay. *(pins ask-8)*
- `an_adopted_unit_the_stack_never_declared_is_not_retired`: A unit registered by `homelab adopt` that the stack file never declared is not the deploy's to retire. *(pins ask-8)*
- `a_mount_the_stack_no_longer_declares_is_detached_and_its_directory_kept`: `Loskoppelen`: `pct set --delete mpN` under lifted protection; the host directory stays. *(pins ask-8)*
- `a_removed_app_keeps_its_vault_copy_and_records_when_it_left`: `Samen met de back-up`: the deletion policy is not decided, so the deploy deletes nothing from the vault and records when the app left. *(pins ask-8)*
- `a_destroyed_stack_is_recorded_with_everything_it_left_behind`: Kenny, 2026-09-27 (ask-9): backups, /appdata and vault copies of a destroyed stack are kept forever by default — so the destroy records exactly what it left behind, and an app that had left the stack earlier is folded into the stack's record. *(pins ask-9)*
- `a_forgotten_stack_is_recorded_as_retired_too` *(pins ask-9)*
- `a_redeployed_stack_is_no_longer_retired`: A stack deployed again is no longer retired. *(pins ask-9)*
- `the_fleet_check_names_what_is_kept_for_every_retired_entry` *(pins ask-9)*
- `the_wipe_plan_lists_exactly_what_goes_and_what_is_still_in_use` *(pins ask-9)*
- `wipe_deletes_the_repositories_directories_and_vault_then_the_record` *(pins ask-9)*
- `wipe_refuses_without_the_typed_name_or_for_a_live_stack` *(pins ask-9)*
- `a_removed_apps_files_are_left_for_the_garbage_collector`: An app that left the stack is the garbage collector's: its compose file must still be there when `docker compose down` runs, or its containers keep running with nothing left to stop them by. *(pins ask-8)*
- `a_stack_that_drops_its_last_manual_question_loses_it`: Found by the documentation pass the same day: the deploy only re-registered manual questions when the stack still had at least one, so a stack that dropped its LAST `manual:` line kept the old question in `homelab checks` until it was destroyed. *(pins step-22)*

### deploy_tests

`core/tests/deploy_tests.rs` · 112 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test deploy_tests`

The M0 safety and idempotency suite — every scenario here maps to a FEATURES.md test scenario (A1, A2, A3/D10, B1, D1, A5).

Findings these tests pin:

- **F107**: The two places where a deploy reads the backup repository built their own `BackupCfg::default()`.
- **F124**: A pushed unit file overwrote almanac's binary, and the service kept reporting itself healthy.
- **F129**: The registry cache answers its probe and still cannot serve.
- **F130**: A truncated blob poisons the direct pull too.
- **F133**: The reconciliation check was written stricter than the deploy is willing to be.
- **F137**: A data directory owned by a uid the application does not use.
- **F141**: cloudflared's data directory was owned by a user it does not run as.
- **F143**: The ownership check I shipped this afternoon was confidently wrong on the first stack it met.
- **F144**: The ownership check was confidently wrong a third time, on a third shape.
- **F145**: Four attempts at inferring which user writes a service's data, four confident wrong answers in one afternoon.
- **F146**: The write probe reported a distroless image as unable to write.
- **F147**: The reconciliation pass called a healthy stack broken.
- **F159**: Grafana was down for four minutes because a bind mount cannot be nested inside a read-only bind mount.
- **F164**: Nine of ten containers report no container metrics, and the guard that should install them has been reporting success the whole time.
- **F169**: Every file bound for a container is staged through one fixed path on the host.
- **F170**: A mount declared in a manifest but never deployed fails the whole stack's backup, with a message that names the wrong problem.
- **F173**: The registry cache has no expiry, and is backed up.
- **F21**: `pct clone` does not take `--unprivileged`, and the golden template CT 999 is unprivileged.
- **F210**: Three brakes that had never been pressed, and one silent skip.
- **F213**: Two update features that had never once run.
- **F22**: Every test in the suite uses `unprivileged: true`; the privileged path has no coverage at all.
- **F289**: De schrijfproef van de deploy noemde een oorzaak die hij niet gemeten had.
- **fix-24**: Traefik's access log has not been rotated since 2026-09-01.
- **fix-27**: A gateway deploy that restarts Loki fails its own service check.
- **fix-28**: A deploy of the kyu stack would install the LATEST release of every native service, whatever its `update_policy` says.
- **fix-37**: Two native units shared one vault copy of their token.
- **fix-39**: Every deploy of a native stack wrote its secrets into the transcript.
- **fix-40**: A changed script under an app was not reloaded when its compose file changed too.

Tests:

- `a_clone_refuses_a_privilege_level_the_template_cannot_give`: A clone can never change a container's privilege level, so asking for one the template cannot give must stop the deploy rather than silently produce the other. *(pins F21, F22)*
- `a_privileged_stack_cloning_the_privileged_template_is_allowed`: And the matching case passes: a privileged stack cloning the privileged template is exactly how the media and downloader stacks are built. *(pins F22)*
- `o7_config_paths_must_be_named_after_their_app`: O7: a config path must be named `<app>-config`.
- `a_mount_inside_a_read_only_mount_is_refused`: A bind mount inside a READ-ONLY bind mount of the same service is refused; inside a writable one it is fine. *(pins F159)*
- `o5_host_owner_uid_must_match_the_privilege_level`: O5: on an unprivileged container uid 1000 inside is uid 101000 on the host, so the two privilege levels need host_owner_uid values 100000 apart.
- `a1_no_touch_vmid_is_refused_with_zero_commands`
- `a2_hostname_mismatch_refuses_reuse`
- `d10_path_traversal_is_refused_before_any_command`
- `d10_validator_collects_all_problems`
- `a_bind_inside_a_declared_mount_is_covered_by_it`: A bind INSIDE a declared mount is covered by it.
- `a_deploy_installs_the_unit_file_and_starts_a_service_that_is_down`: Kenny's N1 (2026-08-31): the unit file lives in the repository and a deploy puts it there. *(pins F124)*
- `a_running_native_service_whose_unit_and_env_are_unchanged_is_not_restarted`: A service that is already running, whose unit file and env file are what the deploy would write, is left running.
- `fix_159_a_changed_unit_restarts_the_running_service_with_a_health_check`: fix-159 (2026-09-29): HOMELAB_ADMIN_LIVE_ANNOUNCE_MS=5000 went into admin.service at 05:41 and took effect at the 13:28 reinstall: the deploy wrote the unit and reloaded systemd, and the running service kept its old settings.
- `fix_159_a_changed_env_file_restarts_the_running_service`: fix-159: the env file changed under a running unit (here: it was gone and the vault copy came back), so the unit restarts to read it.
- `fix_159_a_restart_that_does_not_come_up_fails_the_deploy`: fix-159: a restart that does not come up healthy fails the deploy with what, why and the reading, instead of being recorded as done.
- `a_declared_unit_without_its_file_is_refused`: A declared unit with no unit file is refused, loudly.
- `native_only_lets_a_container_declare_that_it_runs_no_docker`: Kenny asked the right question on 2026-08-31: the four native services could be backed up and updated, but nothing in the repository said how to rebuild the container they run on.
- `a_native_only_container_is_never_given_docker`: Such a container must never be given docker: installing it would change the very thing the manifest exists to reproduce.
- `m1_a_borrowed_directory_is_mounted_but_never_created`: The media libraries are two ZFS datasets that Proxmox hands to the fileserver and to the media container at the same time.
- `m1_a_missing_borrowed_directory_stops_the_deploy`: A missing one is refused.
- `m1_the_two_kinds_of_directory_cannot_be_confused`: The two lists stay distinct, in both directions.
- `m1_a_stack_without_borrowed_directories_is_never_probed`: A stack with no borrowed directories must not be asked about any.
- `a_missing_mount_is_reattached_on_an_existing_container`: A mount that is missing from a live container is put back by a deploy.
- `protection_is_put_back_when_the_stack_file_asks_for_it`: The protection flag is intent like any other, and it was only ever set on the run that created the container.
- `matching_mounts_are_left_completely_alone`: A container whose mounts already match is not written to at all, and its protection flag is never touched.
- `w3_a_deploy_puts_a_drifted_boot_policy_back`: The W3 acceptance criterion's second half: a boot order moved by hand is corrected by a deploy.
- `w3_a_container_that_agrees_is_not_written_to`: A container that already agrees is left alone — the check must not produce a write on every deploy.
- `w1_a_gpu_stack_is_refused_when_the_host_has_no_card`: F54, the most self-concealing failure left in the fleet: a stack with `gpu: true` on a host with no card comes up perfectly and transcodes on the CPU.
- `w1_the_device_group_ids_are_read_from_the_host`: The other half of F54: the group ids were the literals 44 and 104, right on this host and silently wrong on any other.
- `w1_a_vpn_stack_is_refused_when_the_host_has_no_tun`: The same shape for the VPN flag: without /dev/net/tun the container starts and only the tunnel inside it fails, where nothing is looking.
- `w1_a_stack_without_hardware_is_never_probed`: A stack that asks for no hardware must not be probed at all — a check that runs where it has no business is a check that can refuse a deploy for a reason that does not apply to it.
- `m7_a_replaced_stack_recovers_its_backup_time_from_the_repository`: A C4 replacement destroys the container and its state record together, so "preserve the previous value" preserves nothing.
- `a_deploy_never_unregisters_the_native_services_on_its_stack`: The native services registered on a stack are not the deploy's to forget.
- `m7_a_stack_with_no_snapshots_records_zero_and_still_deploys`: The other direction, which is what makes the test above mean anything: a stack whose repository has nothing to say still records a zero, and the deploy still succeeds.
- `m7_a_plain_redeploy_keeps_its_record_without_asking_restic`: A redeploy over a container that still exists keeps the value it already had, and must not spend a restic round trip finding that out.
- `e3_auto_restore_reads_the_configured_repository`: The repository that deploy reads must be the one the host is configured with. *(pins F107)*
- `d1_fresh_deploy_command_sequence`
- `t52_a_changed_config_file_restarts_its_app`: T52: pushing a config file is not the same as the service reading it.
- `t52_a_changed_compose_file_does_not_restart_twice`: The other half: when only the compose file changed, `up -d` recreates the container by itself and a restart on top of that is pure churn.
- `fix_40_a_compose_change_that_recreates_nothing_still_restarts_for_a_changed_script`: fix-40: the compose file AND a bind-mounted script changed, but the compose change was a comment, so `up -d` recreated nothing. *(pins fix-40)*
- `fix_40_a_container_compose_recreated_is_not_restarted_again`: fix-40, the other half: when compose says it recreated the container, the new script is already loaded and a restart would be churn. *(pins fix-40)*
- `fix_40_a_container_older_than_its_files_is_restarted_even_when_nothing_was_pushed`: fix-40, the invariant behind it: a container that started before a file in its app directory last changed is running an older version of that file, whatever this deploy pushed. *(pins fix-40)*
- `t56_a_private_registry_is_signed_into_before_the_pull`: T56: an image behind a login must not need a step nobody wrote down.
- `t56_a_stack_without_a_registry_never_logs_in`: A stack with no private registry must not gain a login step it never asked for.
- `b1_second_run_is_quiet`
- `a5_env_goes_to_vault_never_to_repo`
- `h1_gateway_route_only_to_the_gateway`
- `f129_a_cache_that_cannot_serve_falls_back_to_the_real_registry`: F129 · the fallback half of C1: a cache that answers its probe but cannot serve a blob must not be able to hold the deploy hostage. *(pins F129, F130)*
- `s2_a_failed_redeploy_marks_the_step_without_rewriting_what_applied`: S2b · a stack ALREADY on record whose redeploy stops half-way.
- `s2_a_failed_deploy_still_records_the_stack`: S2a · a deploy that stops half-way must still leave a record.
- `s2_a_refused_target_records_nothing_at_all`: S2a-bis · but a refusal is not a half-deploy.
- `s2_reconcile_catches_a_container_that_does_not_match`: S2b · the reconciliation pass rejects a deploy whose steps all succeeded but whose container does not match the stack file. *(pins F133, F147)*
- `s2_a_push_that_did_not_land_fails_its_own_step`: S2c · a push that reports success and did not land fails its own step, not three steps later.
- `storage_the_app_cannot_write_fails_the_deploy`: Can the application write its own data? That, and nothing about uids. *(pins F137, F141, F143, F144, F145)*
- `storage_the_app_can_write_says_nothing`: And it must stay quiet when the app CAN write, whatever the uids happen to be — the half that decides whether a check survives a month. *(pins F146)*
- `storage_a_container_that_is_not_running_is_reported_as_unmeasured`: T81 (F289): a container that is not running cannot be probed, and the step says so instead of reading the failed exec as a permissions fault. *(pins F289)*
- `storage_a_directory_the_app_does_not_mount_is_skipped`: A directory the app does not mount is not its business. *(pins F146)*
- `gap14_the_monitor_list_carries_adopted_native_stacks`: gap-14: the seeder called `host · kyu` and `host · almanac` monitors of stacks the fleet does not have, because the generated list came only from stacks with a stack manifest in state — and an adopted native stack has none.
- `h4_cadvisor_is_installed_by_the_guards_on_every_docker_host`: H4 · cAdvisor is installed on every managed docker host, not declared per stack.
- `h4_cadvisor_is_started_even_when_its_compose_file_is_unchanged`: And it must bring cadvisor up even when the compose file is ALREADY there. *(pins F164)*
- `h4_cadvisor_is_not_installed_where_there_is_no_docker`: And never on a container that runs no docker: a weekly prune timer on a native-only host has been failing every week since it was installed, which is worse than useless — a guard that fails on schedule teaches you to ignore failures.
- `a_staging_path_is_unique_per_target_file`: T74: two files bound for two different containers must not share a staging path on the host. *(pins F169)*
- `a_path_declared_reproducible_gets_no_repository`: A path declared reproducible gets no restic repository at all. *(pins F173)*
- `switching_a_backup_off_requires_saying_why`: The flag cannot be set without a reason a person can still read later.
- `a_declared_path_that_is_not_there_yet_says_deploy_first`: Z5: a declared path that is not on disk yet gets a message that names the real problem. *(pins F170)*
- `a_vmid_that_is_a_qemu_vm_is_refused_even_when_it_is_not_on_the_list`: Every existing test mocks `qm status` as FAILED, so this branch — the one that refuses to touch a QEMU VM at all — had never been executed. *(pins F210)*
- `fix_130_a_stack_whose_every_mount_is_excluded_backs_up_nothing`: fix-130 (expert panel, doctor-checks-too-little, 2026-09-27): doctor said `registry backup — last backup 12h ago` for a stack that keeps nothing.
- `fix_120_a_privileged_container_outside_the_host_policy_is_refused`: fix-120 (expert panel, api-token-is-root, 2026-09-27): the API token is root on pve as long as a stack file may ask for a privileged container or bind any host path into one.
- `fix_120_a_data_mount_outside_the_host_roots_is_refused`: fix-120: a data mount may only borrow a directory the host names, and a `..` cannot climb out of one.
- `a_route_filename_may_not_climb_out_of_the_routes_directory`: The path-traversal guard on the ONE sanctioned cross-stack write. *(pins F210)*
- `the_update_labels_the_code_reads_exist_somewhere_in_the_fleet`: G2 of the Phase-7 gate. *(pins F213)*
- `a_deploy_registers_the_questions_only_a_person_can_answer`: G17 · a deploy that prints a manual check must also register it.
- `fix_146_an_empty_native_unit_is_restored_before_it_starts`
- `fix_146_a_unit_with_data_is_left_as_it_is`
- `fix_146_a_unit_archived_from_its_own_copy_is_restored_and_left_stopped`
- `fix_147_a_native_check_that_fails_is_remembered`: fix-147: a native unit whose backup could not be checked is remembered as well, keyed by stack and unit.
- `fix_28_a_deploy_never_replaces_an_installed_native_binary`: fix-28: the client stages the NEWEST release of every native; a deploy that found the program already there used to replace it, whatever the service's update_policy said. *(pins fix-28)*
- `fix_28_a_missing_native_binary_is_still_installed`: fix-28: where there is no program yet, the deploy still installs one — a rebuilt container must come back whole. *(pins fix-28)*
- `the_missing_account_is_created_before_anything_starts`
- `a_unit_whose_program_is_absent_is_not_started_and_the_reason_is_named`
- `a_missing_env_file_is_restored_from_the_vault_rather_than_invented`
- `fix_39_a_secret_file_read_for_the_vault_never_reaches_the_transcript`: fix-39: keeping the vault current read each native unit's env file with `cat` through the tracing executor, which echoes a command's output into the transcript. *(pins fix-39)*
- `fix_37_two_units_with_the_same_file_name_keep_separate_vault_copies`: fix-37: the vault named a unit's file by its basename only, so two units reading `token.env` shared ONE vault file and the vault kept whichever was copied last. *(pins fix-37)*
- `fix_37_an_ambiguous_old_flat_vault_copy_is_not_restored`: fix-37: the flat copy an older deploy left behind is ambiguous when two units share the file name, so it is never restored into either; a named missing file beats a unit started with the other one's token. *(pins fix-37)*
- `a_flat_vault_copy_no_unit_would_restore_from_is_removed`: Expert panel 2026-09-27 (stale-secret-residue-on-pve): flat vault copies older deploys wrote stayed on pve with live tokens nothing restores.
- `fix_37_an_unambiguous_old_flat_vault_copy_is_still_restored`: fix-37: a single unit's file keeps being restored from the flat copy an older deploy wrote, so the change of vault layout loses nothing. *(pins fix-37)*
- `a_secret_that_exists_nowhere_stops_the_start_instead_of_looping`
- `fix_145_a_native_stack_declared_unmeasured_gets_no_scrape_target`: fix-145 (expert panel 2026-09-27, inbox-ct118-unmanaged): inbox gets a container file, and Kenny's "Grenzen zetten" (Phase 9 form, 2026-09-27) says Prometheus does not measure it (`metrics: false` in its service.yml).
- `f307_security_updates_are_matched_by_codename_not_by_archive_alias`: F307: the security matcher must key on the codename, never on the archive alias Debian rewrites as a release ages.
- `a_template_name_reports_the_os_it_was_baked_from`: The template's name must say which OS is inside it.
- `a_gateway_deploy_renders_the_receiver_and_restores_single_file_mode`: gap-11 · the deploy renders the gateway's syslog receiver into the one file Alloy reads, and puts Alloy back to reading that one file.
- `an_image_that_is_present_is_not_pulled_and_the_app_still_comes_up`
- `an_image_that_is_missing_is_pulled_as_before`
- `no_answer_about_the_images_means_pull`: Standing rule 12: defaults fail closed.
- `fix_24_the_rotation_rule_renames_and_signals_or_falls_back_to_copytruncate` *(pins fix-24)*
- `fix_24_a_deploy_installs_the_rule_inside_the_container` *(pins fix-24)*
- `fix_24_a_rotation_value_that_would_reach_a_shell_is_refused` *(pins fix-24)*
- `fix_24_the_gateway_rotates_traefiks_access_log` *(pins fix-24)*
- `fix_27_a_restarted_app_warming_up_is_read_again_not_reported` *(pins fix-27)*
- `fix_27_a_change_that_does_not_settle_is_still_reported` *(pins fix-27)*
- `a_deploy_grants_alloy_read_access_and_says_so_when_it_still_cannot_read`: Expert panel 2026-09-27 (container-logs-missing-in-loki): for 24 days Alloy ran on every compose container without being able to open a single container log, and every deploy said nothing.
- `docker_keeps_containers_running_across_its_own_restart`: Expert panel 2026-09-27 (docker-no-live-restore): every change to daemon.json restarts docker, and without live-restore that stops every container on the machine with it.
- `unattended_upgrades_also_take_alloy_from_grafanas_repository`: Kenny's triage answer 2026-09-27 (alloy-not-updated-loki-stale-pin: "Alloy automatisch"): unattended-upgrades took only Debian security, so Alloy, installed from Grafana's signed repository, stayed on 1.19.2 while 1.20.0 was out (measured on CT 106 the same evening).
- `a_deploy_refuses_a_container_short_of_memory`: Correction corr-kuma-memory (Kenny: Klopt, 2026-09-27).
- `memory_headroom_is_read_from_meminfo`
- `a_path_with_a_quote_a_dotdot_or_an_empty_segment_is_refused`: A path lands between single quotes in a root shell on the Proxmox host (`ls -A '<host_path>'`), and in `pct set -mpN <host>,mp=<ct>`.
- `a_value_with_a_quote_is_escaped_in_the_script`: The quoting helper is the only way a value enters a script: a quote inside the value is escaped instead of ending the quoted word.
- `a_failed_staleness_probe_restarts_rather_than_assuming_fresh`: Standing rule 12: no usable answer is not "no".
- `a_compose_warning_mentioning_created_does_not_skip_the_restart`: fix-40 skipped the restart when compose's output contained "reated", which also matches a warning that a volume "was not created by Docker Compose".
- `a_failed_removal_of_a_dropped_app_is_not_reported_as_removed`: The garbage collector threw the exit code of its removal away and logged "removed" anyway.
- `fix_141_a_deploy_records_the_commit_and_the_uncommitted_files`: fix-141 (expert panel 2026-09-27, changes-reach-prod-without-ci): every intent commit said only `deploy <stack>`, so "which commit is deployed on CT 104?" had no answer, and a stack deployed from files in no commit looked like any other.
- `fix_141_a_deploy_without_a_source_records_none`: fix-141: a client that does not say where the files came from still deploys, and the record says nothing rather than something invented.

### devicebackup_tests

`core/tests/devicebackup_tests.rs` · 4 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test devicebackup_tests`

Route A (Kenny, form J1 via the OPNsense session, 2026-09-02): the orchestrator asks a device it may not touch for its own configuration and stores the answer in restic.

Findings these tests pin:

- **F205**: The backup credential authenticates and is refused on every endpoint it needs.

Tests:

- `the_credential_never_reaches_the_command_line`: The credential must never reach argv: `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` is world-readable, and this one can download a router's entire configuration. *(pins F205)*
- `a_snapshot_too_small_to_be_a_configuration_fails`: A login page is a 200 with a body, and restic stores whatever it is handed. *(pins F205)*
- `an_unverified_certificate_is_used_but_never_quietly`: Verification is configuration-dependent (rule 24), so the code cannot enforce it — but it must not be silent about running without it. *(pins F205)*
- `a_pinned_public_key_is_what_verifies_the_connection`: The pin is what verifies this connection, and it must reach curl exactly. *(pins F205)*

### facts_tests

`core/tests/facts_tests.rs` · 23 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test facts_tests`

G6 · the fact gatherer, driven through a mock fleet.

Findings these tests pin:

- **fix-104**: Long silent waits.
- **fix-90**: Loki and Grafana shared the gateway's cgroup with Traefik.
- **fix-93**: Loki answered anyone on the LAN, allowed deletes, and ran a 2024 release.
- **gap-27**: Found by the Phase 8 rewrites (step-18), 2026-09-27.
- **gap-33**: Found by the Phase 8 rewrites (step-18), 2026-09-27.
- **step-20**: Deployment project enters Phase 9 (release & lifecycle), 2026-09-27.

Tests:

- `fix_104_the_fact_gatherer_reports_each_phase_as_it_goes`: long-silences (expert panel, 2026-09-27): `homelab check` took 41 s with nothing on the screen after "link up". *(pins fix-104)*
- `g6_pct_list_becomes_vmid_and_hostname_pairs`
- `g6_a_growth_probe_that_never_ran_is_no_fact`: The `guards` line is the proof the probe ran inside the container.
- `g6_host_memory_is_five_numbers_in_the_script_order`
- `g6_the_logs_window_only_passes_digits_and_a_unit`
- `g6_managed_containers_are_probed_and_the_untouchable_are_not`: Containers come from `pct list`; the untouchable ones are never probed; a stopped guest that answers nothing produces no growth fact but still a boot fact, because a stopped guest's configuration can still be read.
- `g6_routes_are_read_from_the_gateway_and_knocked_on`: Every route fragment on the gateway is read, its target extracted, and the target knocked on from inside the gateway with bash's /dev/tcp.
- `g6_a_watched_backup_is_aged_against_now_and_a_failed_listing_is_an_error`: O1: a watched backup's age is the difference between now and the newest file rclone lists; a listing that fails is an error, not an old backup.
- `g6_the_seed_verdict_comes_from_last_seed_json_beside_the_monitors`: T49: the seeder's verdict is read from the file beside the monitor list; no configured file means nothing to judge, which is not a finding.
- `g6_coverage_asks_prometheus_per_recorded_stack_and_leaves_loki_unasked`: Coverage is asked only where an address is configured, per recorded stack; Prometheus' answer is read for a `1`, and an unconfigured Loki leaves the logs question unasked rather than answered.
- `g6_an_empty_fleet_yields_empty_facts_not_findings`: Nothing configured, nothing recorded: the gatherer still returns, with every unasked question absent rather than failed.
- `step_20_a_service_declared_unmeasured_is_not_asked_and_is_noted`: inbox-guards (Kenny, Phase 9 form 2026-09-27): a native service whose service.yml says `metrics: false` is deliberately not measured. *(pins step-20)*
- `gap_27_a_secret_file_without_a_vault_copy_is_named_unsealed`: gap-27 (Kenny, Phase 9 form 2026-09-27: "Echt maken"): the doctor's env check was fed "sealed" for every stack and could never fire. *(pins gap-27)*
- `gap_33_a_container_without_docker_needs_only_the_journald_cap`: gap-33 follow-up: a container without docker is guarded by the journald cap alone. *(pins gap-33)*
- `coverage_asks_loki_for_every_stack_without_a_promtail_app`: Expert panel 2026-09-27 (container-logs-missing-in-loki): the coverage check only asked Loki about stacks listing an app named `promtail`, and since the fleet moved to Alloy (2026-09-02) no stack does, so the check never fired while no container line arrived for 24 days.
- `fix_90_the_dashboard_question_is_asked_where_grafana_runs`: fix-90 (2026-09-27, gateway-shared-no-limits): Grafana runs on the metrics container now, so the question which generated dashboards it serves is asked there, not on the gateway. *(pins fix-90)*
- `fix_93_the_log_question_is_asked_inside_lokis_container`: fix-93 (expert panel 2026-09-27, loki-unauthenticated-open): the LAN port takes pushes only, so the host can no longer read Loki from outside. *(pins fix-93)*
- `fix_142_the_intent_copy_is_read_file_by_file`: fix-142 (expert panel 2026-09-27, check-blind-to-repo-drift): the host's intent-history copy of each stack the client named, hashed file by file, so the check can say which files differ.
- `speed_a_check_with_recorded_backups_asks_no_remote`: Decision "Fleet check speed" (2026-09-29, backup-read = reuse): the check reads the watched backups the host recorded and asks rclone nothing.
- `speed_a_check_without_a_record_asks_once_and_records_it`: No record yet (the first check after the upgrade, or a watcher moved to another path): asked once, recorded, and the next check asks nothing.
- `speed_the_nightly_round_lists_and_records_but_not_a_failure`: The nightly round always lists, and its answer replaces the record; a listing that fails is reported that night and never recorded.
- `speed_a_device_backup_records_its_watchers`: A device backup this suite made is recorded for the watcher on its repository, in either spelling F259 accepts, and for no other watcher.
- `host_memory_reads_the_config_files_not_pct_config`: Measured on pve 2026-09-29 15:14: `pct config` for each of 19 containers took 9.25 s, the bulk of the fleet check's first stage; the same committed-memory total (38144) reads from the config files in 2 ms.

### firewall_declarations_tests

`core/tests/firewall_declarations_tests.rs` · 5 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test firewall_declarations_tests`

fix-89: the firewall every stack file declares (fix-88), held against the house as it was measured on 2026-09-27.

Findings these tests pin:

- **fix-89**: Which flows each container really needs was written down nowhere, so no firewall could be switched on without guessing.

Tests:

- `kp_soft_declares_its_live_firewall_plus_kennys_kuma_rule`: CT 116's declaration renders to the file on pve (captured byte for byte on 2026-09-27) with exactly three differences: the provenance line on top, the rule Kenny added that day letting Uptime Kuma's HTTP monitor in (form item kp-soft-kuma-firewall: "Kuma HTTP toelaten, firewall in de repo"), and the Loki push going to the metrics stack (10.10.10.13) instead of the gateway, where Loki no longer runs since fix-90 (2026-09-28: without it CT 116's Alloy would push into a closed port). *(pins fix-89)*
- `every_stack_declares_a_firewall_and_only_kp_soft_enables_it`: Every compose stack declares a firewall, and only kp-soft's and admin's are switched on. *(pins fix-89)*
- `the_gateway_declaration_opens_port_80_to_nobody`: traefik-lan-host-header-bypass: the gateway's declaration opens port 80 to nobody, so switching it on closes the Host-header route to the Proxmox and OPNsense logins. *(pins fix-89)*
- `every_measured_flow_passes_the_declared_firewalls_at_both_ends`: Every measured flow passes the declared firewall at both ends, read the way Proxmox reads it — including the declarations not yet enabled, which is the point: they are switched on later, one at a time, and must not break a real connection on that day. *(pins fix-89)*
- `the_logins_stay_out_of_reach_from_the_neighbours`: And what the findings are about stays shut once a stack is switched on: no neighbour reaches Traefik's port 80 (the Host-header route to the logins), and no container but the ones that declare it reaches pve's or OPNsense's GUI. *(pins fix-89)*

### firewall_tests

`core/tests/firewall_tests.rs` · 12 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test firewall_tests`

fix-88 (expert panel 2026-09-27, flat-vlan-no-east-west-control and traefik-lan-host-header-bypass): a container's Proxmox firewall is declared in its stack file, rendered by a pure function, written by the deploy only when it changed, and held against pve by the fleet check.

Findings these tests pin:

- **fix-154**: A rebuilt kp-soft came up without its firewall rules.
- **fix-88**: No container had a firewall of its own except CT 116, and that one was hand-made.

Tests:

- `the_renderer_reproduces_the_hand_made_116_fw_byte_for_byte`: The renderer reproduces the hand-made 116.fw byte for byte (the captured copy was compared with pve's by `cmp` on 2026-09-27 and is identical), plus one provenance line. *(pins fix-88)*
- `the_management_network_is_closed_after_the_declared_rules_unless_opened_with_a_reason`: Without `management_open`, the renderer appends the management guard after the declared rules: DNS to the router, nothing else on 10.10.5.0/24. *(pins fix-88)*
- `a_declaration_proxmox_would_misread_is_refused_with_the_rule_named`: A declaration the renderer cannot honour is refused before anything is written, each problem naming the rule and the field, with the remedy. *(pins fix-88)*
- `the_gateway_may_not_open_port_80_to_its_neighbours`: traefik-lan-host-header-bypass: Traefik answers a forged Host header with the Proxmox and OPNsense logins (measured from CT 107, 2026-09-27). *(pins fix-88)*
- `a_deploy_writes_the_firewall_only_when_it_changed_and_says_so`: Written only when the rendering differs from what pve holds, and the transcript says which: unchanged, or exactly which lines came and went. *(pins fix-88)*
- `a_new_container_is_created_behind_its_firewall`: A new container starts behind its firewall: the file is written before the container exists and the NIC is created with `firewall=1`. *(pins fix-88)*
- `fix_154_the_firewall_is_written_again_after_the_container_is_created`: fix-154 (2026-09-28 07:09, the Debian 13 rebuild of kp-soft): the file written before the container existed was gone once `pct clone` had made CT 116 — Proxmox drops a vmid's firewall file when it creates that vmid — so the one container strangers reach came up with `firewall=1` on its NIC and no rules at all. *(pins fix-154)*
- `an_enabled_firewall_switches_the_nic_flag_on_and_keeps_the_rest_of_net0`: An existing container whose NIC has the flag off gets it switched on, with every other part of its net0 (the MAC address above all) kept as it was. *(pins fix-88)*
- `a_declaration_that_is_not_enabled_changes_nothing_on_pve`: `enabled: false` is a declaration kept for the rollout, not applied: no file, no NIC change, and the transcript says so. *(pins fix-88)*
- `the_gateway_deploy_refuses_a_firewall_that_opens_port_80`: On the gateway, a rule opening port 80 is refused before anything is written, which is what closes the Host-header route to the logins. *(pins fix-88)*
- `the_fleet_check_reports_a_firewall_file_that_differs_from_its_declaration`: `homelab check` holds every managed container's `.fw` on pve against its declaration: a hand edit, a missing file, a NIC with the flag off and a file the repository does not declare are each a finding with a remedy; declarations kept for the rollout are noted in one line. *(pins fix-88)*
- `the_facts_read_every_recorded_stacks_firewall_file`: The gatherer reads each recorded stack's file off pve, and says absent when there is none. *(pins fix-88)*

### fleetcheck_tests

`core/tests/fleetcheck_tests.rs` · 68 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test fleetcheck_tests`

Y4: the fleet check has one job — find the things that look healthy.

Findings these tests pin:

- **F149**: Every generated Grafana dashboard has been written into a directory nothing reads.
- **F184**: The fleet check gave eight containers advice the machine cannot follow.
- **F198**: The router backs itself up and nobody was watching.
- **F211**: Two fleet-check branches nobody had ever run.
- **F214**: The nightly check skipped the nights it mattered most, and the rule deciding what counts as an alarm was untestable.
- **F79**: The container name was missing for two independent reasons on one line.
- **fix-103**: `homelab check` buried its one real problem and mixed history into the remedies.
- **fix-24**: Traefik's access log has not been rotated since 2026-09-01.
- **fix-26**: kyu-runner's state directory was owned by root, so kyu-runner could not start again.
- **gap-32**: Found by the Phase 8 rewrites (step-18), 2026-09-27.

Tests:

- `y4_a_healthy_fleet_is_silent`: A healthy fleet produces nothing.
- `y4_finds_the_kyu_case`: The kyu case, exactly: the record still describes the pre-rename hostname, so every operation fails the guard, the nightly run failed, H8 disabled the stack, and it had never been backed up.
- `y4_finds_a_vanished_container`: A container removed outside the orchestrator leaves a record pointing at nothing.
- `y4_finds_a_stack_file_aimed_at_someone_elses_container`: The stacks/cloudflared case: a file claiming vmid 109, which was kyu.
- `y4_finds_routes_that_lead_nowhere`: Both dead routes: the one to the empty MQTT container and the one to Kenny's own workstation.
- `y4_finds_a_backup_that_quietly_stopped`: A backup that stopped is not visible from the outside — the files are still there, they are just old.
- `y4_probe_address_covers_every_route_shape_in_the_house`: The probe address, which the first live run got wrong twice.
- `healthy_container_reports_no_growth_findings`: The baseline that makes the rest meaningful: a container inside every limit produces nothing at all.
- `missing_guards_are_reported`: CT 104's shape before the rollout: guards written months earlier that had never run there.
- `docker_logs_and_journal_are_checked_separately`: Loki's 923 MB lived in docker's log directory, not the journal.
- `a_nearly_full_disk_is_broken_not_drift`: A full rootfs is the one growth case that is not merely drift: from here an image pull or an apt upgrade can fail halfway.
- `swap_in_use_is_reported`: CT 106 sat at 1028 MB of swap, which is what prompted G2.
- `limits_are_honoured_rather_than_hardcoded`: The limits are configurable (standing rule 27), so a fleet with different tolerances gets different answers from the same facts.
- `every_container_is_reported_independently`: The check runs over the whole fleet, and one loud container must not mask the others.
- `a_stack_with_no_prometheus_target_is_reported`: A stack nobody is scraping is a stack whose failure nobody will see.
- `a_dashboard_grafana_never_received_is_reported`: The deploy writing a dashboard is not the same question as Grafana having it, and for seven weeks only the first was asked. *(pins F149)*
- `an_unasked_dashboard_question_is_never_a_finding`: And the unasked question must stay unasked. *(pins F149)*
- `a_stack_whose_logs_never_arrive_is_reported`: Logs that go nowhere look exactly like a quiet service — which is why the window this is asked over is a setting and not the hour it started as. *(pins F79)*
- `an_unasked_question_is_never_a_finding`: The rule that keeps this check believable: a question that was not asked must never become a finding.
- `a_covered_stack_is_silent`: A fully covered stack says nothing at all.
- `w3_a_hand_edited_boot_order_is_reported`: The W3 acceptance criterion, first half: a container whose boot order was moved by hand is reported.
- `w3_resources_are_reported_with_the_remedy_that_applies`: Resources diverge with a different remedy, because a deploy deliberately does not change them under a running service.
- `w3_a_container_that_matches_says_nothing`: Agreement is silence, and an unasked question is not a finding: a stack whose record carries no manifest is skipped rather than guessed at.
- `w3_the_repair_touches_boot_policy_and_nothing_else`: The repair side stays as narrow as the reporting side is wide: the arguments a deploy would apply cover boot policy only, never resources.
- `a_swapping_container_on_a_short_host_is_not_told_to_take_more_memory`: F184: a remedy that cannot be carried out is not a remedy. *(pins F184)*
- `a_watched_backup_that_stopped_is_a_finding`: A backup this suite does not make but does watch. *(pins F198)*
- `a_stack_that_clones_a_template_which_is_gone_is_a_finding`: A stack whose golden template no longer exists on the hypervisor. *(pins F211)*
- `a_stack_that_deliberately_keeps_nothing_is_noted_not_broken`: The branch that decides whether "never been backed up" is a fault or a decision. *(pins F211)*
- `a_deliberate_decision_never_raises_the_alarm_but_is_never_hidden_either`: G15 of the Phase-7 gate, the testable half. *(pins F214)*
- `a_finished_deploy_says_nothing`
- `a_deploy_that_stopped_halfway_is_reported_with_the_step_it_stopped_at`
- `the_full_round_carries_it_so_the_nightly_report_does_too`
- `the_full_round_carries_the_manual_checks`: G17: the unanswered question has to ride the round that already reaches Kenny, or it is a record nobody reads — the fault this whole audit is about.
- `only_a_2xx_counts_as_delivered`
- `the_fallback_is_tried_after_the_primary_and_never_twice`
- `a_working_notification_path_is_not_a_finding`
- `a_notification_that_reached_no_route_is_reported_with_what_it_said`
- `a_path_that_never_worked_says_that_rather_than_a_misleading_zero`
- `the_full_round_carries_it`
- `the_full_round_carries_the_restore_drill`: G14: the drill's verdict has to ride the round that already reaches Kenny.
- `the_full_round_carries_the_second_copy_and_the_checks`: fix-96 (single-offsite-copy-no-integrity-check, 2026-09-27): a failed second copy and a failed `restic check` ride the same round.
- `a_recent_run_with_nothing_stale_says_nothing`
- `a_monitor_for_a_stack_that_is_gone_is_named`: The case Kenny found by noticing ping errors on a Grafana panel: a drill container destroyed hours earlier, still pinged every minute.
- `a_seeder_that_stopped_running_is_broken_not_quiet`
- `one_that_has_never_run_says_so_rather_than_looking_healthy`
- `a_run_that_judged_nothing_does_not_read_as_all_clear`: F175's lesson, kept: without a list to compare against, "nothing stale" is not an all-clear.
- `an_unreadable_status_file_is_a_finding_not_a_silence`
- `the_full_round_carries_it`
- `r13_a_pool_with_room_says_nothing`: The state on the night this was written: 30% full, 11.5 TB free.
- `r13_a_filling_pool_is_drift_and_a_nearly_full_one_is_broken`
- `r13_the_finding_carries_the_percentage_and_the_free_space`: Both numbers, always.
- `r13_one_pool_shared_by_two_stacks_is_reported_once`: Two stacks on one pool are one pool.
- `r13_the_defaults_are_quiet_on_the_fleet_as_it_stands`: The thresholds are configuration, not the author's taste (standing rule 27), and the defaults have to open SILENT on this fleet — a check that arrives with findings about pools that are fine teaches everyone to skip the section it lives in.
- `it_reads_the_real_numbers`
- `a_pool_two_stacks_share_names_both_of_them`: The bug this test exists for: CT 105 and CT 106 both mount the 18 TB dataset.
- `a_missing_mount_does_not_shift_every_reading_after_it`: A path that does not exist yields a line with the path and nothing else.
- `a_path_nobody_declared_is_ignored`
- `fix_24_a_log_past_500_mb_is_drift_and_the_remedy_depends_on_its_rule` *(pins fix-24)*
- `fix_26_a_directory_owned_by_someone_else_than_declared_is_drift` *(pins fix-26)*
- `gap_32_noted_findings_alone_do_not_make_the_check_fail`: gap-32: `homelab check` answered "not ok" (exit 1) when the only findings were `noted` ones, which by definition need nothing done; the nightly round already filtered those out with `alarming`. *(pins gap-32)*
- `fix_103_the_check_leads_with_a_summary_and_the_broken_items`: check-output-buries-problem (expert panel, 2026-09-27): live, the header said `9 finding(s)`, two were `[noted]` ("nothing to do"), and the one `[broken]` item was seventh of nine because the list was sorted by subject. *(pins fix-103)*
- `fix_103_remedies_say_what_to_do_not_what_happened`: The same finding: remedies carried rationale and history ("Printing the question at the end of a deploy was how they went unanswered", F-ids). *(pins fix-103)*
- `fix_142_an_edited_but_undeployed_stack_is_drift_and_names_what_differs`: fix-142 (expert panel 2026-09-27, check-blind-to-repo-drift): the check sent only `(dir, vmid)` pairs and never compared the files with what the host applied, so an edited but undeployed stack stayed invisible until the next deploy acted on it.
- `fix_142_a_stack_equal_to_what_was_applied_is_quiet`: fix-142: files equal to what the host applied say nothing.
- `fix_142_a_declared_stack_that_was_never_deployed_is_drift`: fix-142: a stack file the host has never applied is drift too; `apply` would create it (the drill stack's shape, apply-no-confirm-creates-drill).
- `an_on_demand_stack_that_was_never_deployed_is_not_drift`: Kenny, 2026-09-29 (batch form, drill-stack): a stack marked on_demand (the rollback drill, created and destroyed in one sitting) is not reported as never deployed; the real stacks directory marks drill so.
- `fix_142_without_digests_there_is_no_repository_comparison`: fix-142: no digests (an older client, or the nightly round, which has no repository) means no comparison, not "everything changed".
- `fix_142_a_stack_without_a_manifest_compares_its_files_only`: fix-142: a stack with only a `service.yml` sends no manifest; its record has none either, and that is not a difference.

### homeaddress_tests

`core/tests/homeaddress_tests.rs` · 10 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test homeaddress_tests`

fix-94 (Kenny, triage 2026-09-27, crowdsec-home-ip: "Thuisadres automatisch vrijstellen"): since fix-45 CrowdSec sees real visitor addresses, the house's own public one among them (62.235.8.143, measured 2026-09-27). The orchestrator reads the router's WAN address and keeps it in a CrowdSec whitelist on the gateway, so a burst of the house's own traffic can never ban the house.

Findings these tests pin:

- **fix-156**: The house's address was never read.
- **fix-94**: CrowdSec could ban the house's own public address.

Tests:

- `the_whitelist_names_the_address_and_reads_it_back`: The whitelist file is the memory: what it names is the last known address, so it has to read back what it was written with. *(pins fix-94)*
- `a_changed_address_rewrites_the_whitelist_and_reloads_crowdsec`: A new address rewrites the file and reloads CrowdSec, and the log says from what to what. *(pins fix-94)*
- `an_unchanged_address_touches_nothing`: The nightly check runs every night; a reload every night would be noise and a needless risk to the one service whose absence answers 403 to the whole house. *(pins fix-94)*
- `the_first_run_writes_the_whitelist`: First run: no whitelist file yet. *(pins fix-94)*
- `an_unreadable_address_keeps_the_last_known_one`: An address that cannot be read keeps the last known one: nothing is written, nothing removed, CrowdSec is not touched, the operation does not fail (a failed operation notifies, and this is not worth waking anyone for), and the fleet check carries a noted finding that says so. *(pins fix-94)*
- `a_whitelist_crowdsec_refuses_is_put_back`: CrowdSec exits on a reload it cannot load, and the bouncer then answers 403 to everything. *(pins fix-94)*
- `a_readable_address_is_no_finding`: Nothing recorded (never checked, or checked fine) is nothing to report. *(pins fix-94)*
- `fix_156_a_public_service_answer_is_read_and_checked`: fix-156: Cloudflare's trace and ipify's bare answer both read; a private or garbled answer is refused, never whitelisted. *(pins fix-156)*
- `fix_156_ipify_answers_when_cloudflare_does_not`: fix-156: when Cloudflare does not answer, ipify does. *(pins fix-156)*
- `fix_156_no_address_is_broken_a_last_known_one_is_noted`: fix-156: no address at all is broken (the house can be banned and the dashboard refuses it); a last known one is only noted. *(pins fix-156)*

### homepage_tests

`core/tests/homepage_tests.rs` · 13 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test homepage_tests`

T51: the front page rendered from the routes the orchestrator already writes, instead of a file somebody maintains.

Findings these tests pin:

- **F166**: The front page lists nothing, and has for as long as anyone can tell.
- **F188**: T51 generates a file that another mount hides.
- **F190**: I took Uptime Kuma down with a backup file.
- **F195**: The route parser threw away the one field a widget needs.
- **F197**: Two defects in the merge that every test agreed with.
- **F200**: The front page rendered a YAMLException, live, and the third bug of the same family.

Tests:

- `a_route_fragment_yields_its_hostnames_and_its_backends` *(pins F166)*
- `a_stack_without_routes_is_skipped_rather_than_rendered_empty`
- `rendering_twice_produces_the_same_bytes`
- `a_generated_file_takes_the_owner_of_the_directory_it_lands_in`: A generated file lands in a directory that belongs to a CONTAINER, and the orchestrator writes it as host root. *(pins F190)*
- `a_failing_chown_does_not_fail_the_write`: The chown is best-effort: a convenience file must never fail a deploy.
- `the_overlay_supplies_what_a_route_cannot_and_nothing_else`: The real overlay, verbatim from the repo, joined with routes shaped like the ones the gateway actually holds. *(pins F188)*
- `merging_twice_produces_the_same_bytes`: Same input, same bytes — a deploy that changes nothing must report "unchanged" rather than rewrite the file every night.
- `a_widget_is_derived_from_the_route_and_the_application`: Kenny asked whether the live tiles — what is streaming, how many films — could be automatic. *(pins F195)*
- `a_missing_key_still_produces_a_widget`: A key that cannot be read must fail visibly rather than vanish: the tile still gets a widget, pointing at Homepage's own variable, so Homepage reports the problem instead of the widget quietly not being there.
- `a_second_route_to_the_same_door_is_not_a_second_tile`: Not every route is a front door. *(pins F195)*
- `overlay_lines_sit_under_their_service_not_beside_it`: The bug this catches shipped once and no test saw it: every assertion asked whether a line was PRESENT, not where it sat. *(pins F197)*
- `tiles_follow_the_order_written_in_the_overlay`: Media is first because Kenny asked for it, and within Media Jellyfin is first for the same reason. *(pins F197)*
- `the_generated_page_is_valid_yaml`: The test that should have existed from the first line of this generator. *(pins F200)*

C1/C2 · the replacement for a log shipper that reached end of life.

Findings these tests pin:

- **fix-93**: Loki answered anyone on the LAN, allowed deletes, and ran a 2024 release.

Tests:

- `every_label_promtail_set_is_still_set`: The labels are the contract.
- `the_container_name_is_read_from_tag_and_not_from_name`: F72, pinned: docker puts the container's name in `attrs.tag`, and reading `attrs.name` instead is what left three dashboards empty for months.
- `the_journal_is_read_because_on_a_native_container_that_is_the_log`: The half promtail never had on these containers.
- `it_points_at_the_loki_it_was_given_and_nowhere_else`
- `installing_is_idempotent_and_says_so_without_doing_anything`: A deploy runs this every time.
- `fix_152_the_package_lists_are_refreshed_before_the_first_install`: fix-152 (2026-09-28 06:09, the first deploy of inbox on CT 118): the script installed `gpg curl` BEFORE its first `apt-get update`, against package lists from the template build (2025-10-01), so apt asked deb.debian.org for a libssh2 version that had moved on and got 404.
- `the_package_comes_from_a_signed_repository`: The apt route is the point: it is what keeps the shipper patched, which is the whole reason for leaving promtail behind.
- `alloy_is_given_read_access_to_all_three_sources`: A shipper that cannot read the files it is pointed at delivers nothing and reports itself healthy — the fault this whole migration exists to escape.
- `the_config_goes_where_the_packaged_unit_already_looks`
- `the_base_address_becomes_the_push_endpoint`
- `an_address_that_already_names_the_path_is_left_alone`
- `the_generated_config_carries_the_push_path_and_not_the_base`
- `dropped_bytes_mean_the_far_end_refused_them`: The exact state the first live deploy was in while reporting success.
- `sent_bytes_with_none_dropped_is_the_only_good_answer`
- `nothing_either_way_is_reported_as_nothing_either_way`: Nothing sent and nothing dropped is genuinely ambiguous, and saying so beats picking the flattering reading.
- `no_answer_is_not_a_healthy_answer`
- `dropping_outranks_sending`: Dropping wins over sending: a shipper that delivered something and then started losing batches is broken, not fine.
- `several_endpoints_are_summed_rather_than_the_first_one_taken`
- `the_journal_job_label_is_forced_and_not_left_to_alloy`: Alloy names a job after the component that produced it, so the journal arrived as `job="loki.source.journal.journal"` on the first live run.
- `a_declared_receiver_listens_and_labels_its_lines_like_the_hand_made_one_did`: The labels are the contract again: the vault note and the Grafana query both read `{job="syslog", host="opnsense"}`.
- `fix_93_a_receiver_keeps_only_the_senders_it_names`: fix-93 (expert panel 2026-09-27, loki-unauthenticated-open): the receiver took lines from any sender on the LAN, so any container could write lines labelled as the firewall. *(pins fix-93)*
- `a_stack_that_declares_no_receiver_opens_no_port`: Ten other containers render this same file.
- `two_receivers_get_two_distinct_component_names`: Two receivers on one container are two components, and Alloy refuses a file that names one component twice.
- `the_deploy_puts_alloy_back_to_reading_the_one_file_it_renders`: The hand-made change on CT 104 switched Alloy to directory mode (`CONFIG_FILE="/etc/alloy"`), which loads every `*.alloy` in the directory.
- `alloy_gets_read_search_capability_for_the_root_only_docker_directory`: Expert panel 2026-09-27 (container-logs-missing-in-loki): no container log line reached Loki from 2026-09-03 on.
- `readability_is_read_from_the_probe_output`: The deploy asks the question that was never asked: can the alloy user actually list the container log directory?
- `the_readability_probe_asks_about_the_running_service_not_a_new_session`: fix-44 follow-up, measured on the first live deploy (CT 104, 2026-09-27 18:09): the deploy granted the capability and Alloy read eight container logs (`loki_source_file_file_bytes_total` per file, Loki gained the `container_name` label), yet the probe said "cannot read".
- `the_docker_pipeline_drops_the_per_container_filename_label`: Expert panel 2026-09-27 (loki-label-hygiene): `loki.source.file` adds a `filename` label carrying the container's 64-hex id, so every recreate of a container opened new Loki streams for the same app.
- `container_lines_keep_the_time_docker_wrote`: Expert panel 2026-09-27 (docker-log-timestamps-wrong): the docker pipeline used the moment Alloy read a line as its time.

### m4_ops_tests

`core/tests/m4_ops_tests.rs` · 118 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test m4_ops_tests`

M4 operation tests: gated destroy (C2) and backup/restore (E1/E2).

Findings these tests pin:

- **F105**: The empty-snapshot guard was checked against restic itself, not only against its own unit test: a throwaway repository over an empty directory made restic (...)
- **F153**: Every backup this fleet has ever taken ran without a restic cache.
- **F154**: One empty directory stops a whole stack's backup.
- **F156**: The TUI reaches nine of the twenty-five operations the host can perform.
- **F162**: A destroy left the stack's Grafana dashboard behind, and reported that it had removed it.
- **F180**: The host's own configuration file was in no backup at all.
- **F207**: A restore could take a stack down and leave it there, over a typo.
- **F209**: A test whose comment described a test that did not exist.
- **F210**: Three brakes that had never been pressed, and one silent skip.
- **F36**: `native.rs:73` refuses a manifest with empty `data_dirs`, and kyu-runner is deliberately stateless (`DynamicUser=yes`, "no state directory, no disk to protect").
- **F75**: The nightly backup could leave a service switched off, and did.
- **fix-90**: Loki and Grafana shared the gateway's cgroup with Traefik.
- **gap-24**: Found by the Phase 8 rewrites (step-18), 2026-09-27.
- **gap-25**: Found by the Phase 8 rewrites (step-18), 2026-09-27.
- **gap-27**: Found by the Phase 8 rewrites (step-18), 2026-09-27.
- **gap-28**: Found by the Phase 8 rewrites (step-18), 2026-09-27.
- **gap-33**: Found by the Phase 8 rewrites (step-18), 2026-09-27.

Tests:

- `c2_destroy_refuses_wrong_typed_name`
- `c2_destroy_refuses_no_touch_vmid`
- `c2_destroy_refuses_hostname_mismatch`
- `c2_destroy_happy_path_lifts_protection_then_destroys`
- `c2_destroy_removes_the_dashboard_on_the_gateway_not_the_host`: The dashboard a destroy removes lives on the GATEWAY, so the removal has to happen there. *(pins F162)*
- `e1_backup_runs_init_quiesce_snapshot_resume_retention`
- `w2_a_stack_keeps_snapshots_by_its_own_policy`: W2's acceptance criterion: two stacks with different retention produce demonstrably different forget decisions.
- `e1_backup_resumes_every_container_it_paused_even_one_not_in_apps`: The backup must resume exactly what it paused, not what the manifest happens to list. *(pins F75)*
- `e1_backup_with_nothing_to_pause_starts_nothing`: Nothing labelled means nothing stopped and nothing to start back — the step must not invent a bare `docker start` with no arguments. *(pins F75)*
- `every_stack_dashboard_has_an_errors_section`: Every stack dashboard carries its own errors-only section, because Kenny asked for it on every one rather than only on the fleet-wide page — and because a stack deployed next month must get it without anyone remembering to add it.
- `a_path_declared_empty_is_not_backed_up_and_must_really_be_empty`: A restic run over a directory that exists and is empty succeeds, writes a snapshot with nothing in it, and reports success. *(pins F154)*

- `fix_64_a_restore_copies_the_current_data_aside_before_it_writes`: fix-64: when the corruption happened before last night's backup, `latest` is the corruption, and the restore overwrote the only other copy of the data.
- `fix_64_no_room_for_the_safety_copy_refuses_before_anything_stops`: fix-64: no room for the copy refuses the restore before anything stops.

- `b6_failed_update_rolls_back_to_captured_image`
- `a_rollback_of_a_digest_pinned_image_does_not_try_to_tag_it`: fix-82 follow-up (2026-09-27): with images pinned as `name:tag@sha256:…`, `docker tag <id> <ref>` is refused ("refusing to create a tag with a digest reference"), so the rollback failed before it recreated anything.
- `fix_61_an_auto_update_copies_the_apps_data_before_the_new_image_starts`: fix-61 (no-pre-update-snapshot, 2026-09-27): the rollback put the old image back but not the data, and a migrating upgrade that failed its verify left the old binary running against the migrated database with no copy of what was there before.
- `fix_61_a_rolled_back_update_keeps_the_pre_update_copy_and_names_it`: fix-61: a rolled-back update keeps the copy and names it.
- `fix_61_no_copy_without_a_new_image_and_no_update_without_room_for_one`: fix-61: nothing new pulled, nothing copied; and no room means no update.

- `the_journal_cap_ships_with_the_binary_and_restarts_journald_once`: Kenny's choice 2026-09-27 (pve-journal-tokens: "journal begrenzen"): pve's journal was 4 GB back to 2026-04-05 with no limit of its own.

- `o10_an_app_in_use_is_skipped_entirely`: O10 end to end: an app that asks to be left alone while in use is skipped, and nothing is pulled or restarted.
- `o9_stop_first_happens_between_the_pull_and_the_up`: O9: a database is stopped cleanly before its replacement comes up, not killed under itself.

- `o2_the_template_bakes_the_observability_agents`: O2: the agents that were installed by hand on six hosts come from the template now.
- `t2_deploy_provisions_a_dashboard_for_the_stack`: T2: a stack brings its own dashboard.
- `t2_the_generated_dashboard_is_scoped_and_stable`: The generated document has to be worth provisioning: real panels, the Prometheus datasource by uid, and every query scoped to this stack so two stacks never show each other's numbers.

- `o6_restore_is_per_path_not_per_stack`: O6: the auto-restore used to be all-or-nothing — it only ran when EVERY path in `storage:` was empty.
- `e3_env_restored_from_vault_when_client_sends_none`

- `h7_corrupt_state_fails_loud_and_quarantines`

- `fix_51_concurrent_state_updates_are_all_kept`: fix-51 (expert panel, state-writes-race, 2026-09-27): the nightly batch runs three backups at once, and each records its notification outcome with a load-modify-save of state.json outside the op lock.
- `h7_newer_schema_refused_missing_file_is_fresh`

- `h14_every_destroy_step_is_journaled_running_then_done`

- `h19_guards_positive_branch_writes_and_restarts_once`
- `b8_disable_parks_stack_and_clears_onboot`
- `b8_enable_restores_onboot_and_flag`
- `b8_no_touch_vmid_refused`
- `b8_old_state_json_defaults_to_enabled`
- `protection_is_set_after_all_drive_changes`: Live-found on the first protected stack with a bind mount (metrics, 2026-08-29): Proxmox refuses drive changes ("can't update CT 113 drive 'mp0' - protection mode enabled") once the protection flag is set, so protection must be the LAST provisioning act — after resize and every mountpoint — on both the clone and the create path.
- `a_destroy_backs_the_stack_up_before_it_removes_anything`: Kenny asked whether a destroy takes a backup first.
- `a_failed_backup_stops_the_destroy`: And when that backup fails, nothing is destroyed.
- `t66_destroy_removes_the_dashboard_the_deploy_wrote`: T66 · whatever a deploy registers, a destroy has to unregister.
- `t69_a_regressed_check_fails_the_deploy_when_nobody_is_watching`: A reading that fell, with nobody watching: the deploy fails. *(pins F156)*
- `e2_a_failed_restore_still_brings_the_stack_back_up`: G4 of the Phase-7 gate. *(pins F207)*
- `e2_an_unknown_snapshot_id_is_refused_before_anything_is_stopped`: G5. *(pins F207)*
- `t69_an_operator_who_says_yes_lets_the_deploy_finish`: G7 of the Phase-7 gate. *(pins F209)*
- `a_destroy_that_takes_no_backup_always_says_why`: G11 of the Phase-7 gate, third part. *(pins F210)*
- `f280_a_backup_does_not_stop_a_container_somebody_is_watching`: The film wins.
- `f280_an_unanswerable_stack_is_left_alone_as_well`: Fail closed here too: a Jellyfin that cannot answer is treated as watched.
- `f280_an_idle_stack_is_backed_up_exactly_as_before`: And the other side of it: an idle evening backs up exactly as before.
- `f280_a_stack_that_never_asks_is_backed_up_without_a_question`: A stack whose apps carry no busy-check label is not asked at all — no second command per app, and certainly no stack left un-backed-up because a question nobody asked could not be answered.
- `f285_an_owner_another_stack_already_has_is_a_conflict`
- `f285_a_stack_does_not_conflict_with_itself`
- `f285_an_owner_nobody_else_claims_is_fine`
- `f285_the_backup_stops_before_it_touches_the_other_repository`: End to end: the backup refuses before it initialises a repository, so the other stack's history is never opened at all.
- `m_t75_the_backup_phase_says_how_long_it_took`: Minutes and seconds, hours past sixty minutes, never bare seconds above a minute — the house rule for durations, and the number the concurrency setting is judged by.
- `t82_the_stack_recorded_first_keeps_the_repository`: A stack without a state entry is the newcomer; between two recorded stacks the earlier one keeps the repository; a tie favours the caller.
- `t82_the_incumbent_backs_up_and_the_newcomer_is_named`: The live stack's backup goes on when a throwaway stack borrows its app name AFTER it — the six minutes JobTracker had no working backup (F292) were the symmetric guard refusing the wrong side.
- `f274_the_host_meta_snapshot_carries_the_smart_collector`: The SMART collector is installed by this suite on the Proxmox host and lives nowhere under `state_dir`, so the nightly host-meta snapshot walked straight past it.
- `f274_a_host_without_the_collector_still_gets_its_snapshot`: A host that never had the collector is not a broken backup.
- `gap_28_restore_refuses_a_native_unit_instead_of_dropping_its_tar_on_the_host`: gap-28: a native unit's backup is one tar stream (`/<unit>-data.tar`), not a copy of its directories. *(pins gap-28)*
- `gap_24_an_init_failure_other_than_already_exists_stops_the_backup`: gap-24: `restic init` was run and its answer thrown away. *(pins gap-24)*
- `gap_24_an_existing_repository_is_not_an_error`: gap-24: an existing repository answers `init` with "already exists" or "already initialized", which is the normal case every night. *(pins gap-24)*
- `gap_24_a_new_repository_whose_password_does_not_open_host_meta_is_refused`: gap-24: a repository created tonight must open with the same password as host-meta-config. *(pins gap-24)*
- `gap_25_a_failed_pull_stops_the_update_before_anything_is_restarted`: gap-25: a pull that failed inside the container (a registry that is down, a tag that no longer exists) was ignored: `up` then restarted the old image, verify passed, and the report said the app was updated. *(pins gap-25)*
- `gap_33_patch_refuses_a_vmid_whose_hostname_is_not_the_stack_s`: gap-33: `homelab patch` ran apt in every vmid recorded in state without the A2 hostname guard every other mutating operation uses. *(pins gap-33)*
- `gap_33_requested_guards_check_the_hostname_and_skip_docker_on_a_native_stack`: gap-33: guards applied on request (`homelab guards`, TUI `g`) skipped the A2 hostname guard, and always installed the docker guards, which on a native container (CT 109, CT 112) add a weekly prune timer that fails every week. *(pins gap-33)*
- `fix_90_the_dashboard_is_written_where_grafana_runs`: fix-90 (2026-09-27, gateway-shared-no-limits): Grafana left the gateway for the metrics container. *(pins fix-90)*

- `registering_twice_does_not_forget_an_answer`

- `a_question_nobody_ever_answered_is_a_finding`

### mock_executor_tests

`core/tests/mock_executor_tests.rs` · 6 tests · `cargo test -p homelab-core --test mock_executor_tests`

The test double itself (expert panel 2026-09-27, mock-executor-weak-assertions): a negative assertion must not pass merely because a command is rendered differently, and a scripted answer that no longer matches anything must be visible.

Tests:

- `ran_sees_a_verb_however_it_is_rendered`: `calls_containing("pct set").is_empty()` passes for `pct  set` in a host-side `sh -c` script.
- `ran_reads_the_script_a_container_was_given`: Inside a container script the words after `sh -c` are what ran.
- `a_rule_that_never_matched_is_reported`: A rule nothing matched used to fall back to "success, empty output" without a word.
- `a_strict_mock_fails_on_a_rule_that_never_matched`: A strict mock fails the test that leaves a rule unused.
- `a_strict_mock_whose_rules_all_matched_passes`: The positive twin: a strict mock whose every rule matched is quiet.
- `the_compose_model_reads_the_directory_however_it_is_quoted`: The compose model found the app directory as the text between the first two single quotes, so it depended on how deploy.rs happened to quote.
